sources.title: workerd — the Workers runtime, 8,643 stars, C++
Cloudflare outage on November 18, 2025 post mortem
Cloudflare to cut about 20% of its workforce
Cloudflare 8-K, Item 5.02 — Chief Legal Officer resignation

claims.text: The public GitHub organisation holds 575 repositories and six of the ten most recently touched — including the Workers runtime (workerd, C++, 8.6k stars) and workers-sdk — had commits within the last two days, so the open-source presence is live work rather than a shop window.

The company publishes detailed post-mortems on its own outages within a day, and its engineers answer questions in the resulting public threads — useful evidence about how incidents are handled internally.

The May 2026 restructuring is framed by the company itself as a move to an 'AI-first operating model', and the public discussion of it is dominated by whether that framing describes a change in how work is done or a cost cut wearing a strategy label. Worth asking directly in interviews.

gaps.reason: fewer than three independent, dated, first-hand employee accounts were found, so wlb_sentiment is left unset rather than estimated from thread tone
gaps.suggested_fallback: ask the recruiter for two current engineers on the team to speak to, and search for recent conference talks by the hiring team

claims.text: Six consecutive years of revenue growth with no year below 27%: $431m, $656m, $975m, $1.30bn, $1.67bn, $2.17bn (FY2020–FY2025, XBRL).
Cash and equivalents rose from $148m to $944m during FY2025, so the $105–110m cash cost of the 2026 restructuring is comfortably covered.
Net loss narrowed to $79m in FY2024 and widened again to $102m in FY2025, so the trend toward profitability reversed in the most recent year.

The 10-K's own risk factors lead with 'We have a history of net losses and may not be able to achieve or sustain profitability' and 'We have experienced rapid revenue growth, which may not be indicative of our future performance'.

The board carried 306 open roles on 27 August 2026 — sixteen weeks after the company told the SEC it was cutting about 20% of its workforce. Hiring and cutting are running at the same time, which usually means a shift in what is being hired for rather than a freeze.
203 of the 306 open roles are listed as Hybrid and 44 as In-Office, against 44 Distributed and 3 in Remote India: this is a company hiring back toward offices.
Against 5,156 employees at the end of FY2025, 306 open roles is a ~6% expansion of the headcount that remains after a 20% reduction — sizeable, and concentrated in engineering titles.

gaps.reason: this is the first local snapshot for cloudflare.com, so role_repost_count_12m and hiring_velocity_90d cannot be computed yet; the Wayback series for the old board URL has only one usable capture because the board moved hosts
gaps.suggested_fallback: re-run the dossier in three weeks — snapshot.py appends automatically on every run — or try `wayback_jobs.py --url 'job-boards.greenhouse.io/cloudflare*'`

claims.text: On 7 May 2026 Cloudflare told the SEC it expects to cut approximately 20% of its workforce as part of a shift to what it calls an 'agentic AI-first operating model', with charges of $140–150m, substantially complete by the end of Q3 FY2026.

Roughly $105–110m of that charge is cash for notice periods and severance and $35–40m is non-cash share-vesting expense, which dates the bulk of the departures to Q2–Q3 FY2026 rather than a rolling programme.

The Chief Legal Officer resigned in February 2026 after nearly ten years, staying on as a senior adviser, with an internal successor named in the same filing — an orderly transition rather than an abrupt exit.

A global outage on 18 November 2025 drew 1,650 comments on Hacker News and a public post-mortem the same day; reliability incidents at this company are public events, and engineering answers for them in the open.

claims.text: Cloudflare sells network, security and developer-platform services from its own global edge, positioning itself against on-premises hardware vendors and the hyperscalers' equivalents (10-K Item 1, Business).
Revenue reached $2.17bn in FY2025, up 29.9% year on year and compounding at 38% since FY2020 ($431m).
The company has never been profitable on a GAAP basis: operating loss was $207m in FY2025, wider than FY2024's $155m, and it names its history of net losses as its first enumerated risk factor.
R&D spend rose every year from $127m (FY2020) to $512m (FY2025), roughly 24% of revenue — an engineering-heavy cost base, which is where a systems role sits.
Headcount was 5,156 full-time employees at 31 December 2025, of whom 2,452 were outside the United States (10-K, Human Capital Resources).

eng_output_signal.note: 575 public repos, six pushed within 48 hours, including the production Workers runtime

stack_currency.note: Rust/C++/TypeScript edge runtime work; the posting's stack matches what the public repos actually run

revenue_trend.note: +29.9% year on year, 38% CAGR across six annual filings

layoff_events_24m.note: one disclosed workforce reduction (May 2026); no Item 2.05 filing in the preceding 24 months

narrative.summary: Cloudflare is a fast-growing infrastructure company that has never turned a GAAP profit and announced a ~20% workforce reduction in May 2026, framed as a move to an AI-first operating model. The balance sheet comfortably absorbs the $105–110m cash cost, and the board still carried 306 open roles in August 2026, so this is a re-shaping rather than a retreat. The engineering work is real and public: the Workers runtime and SDK are developed in the open and were committed to this week. The open question is which side of that re-shaping the team behind this posting sits on.

strengths.text: Six straight years of 27%+ revenue growth, most recently $2.17bn (+29.9%)
Cash grew to $944m in FY2025, so the restructuring is affordable without new financing
Engineering happens in public — 575 repos, the production Workers runtime among them, actively committed
R&D at ~24% of revenue means the systems work is the product, not a cost centre

concerns.text: A 20% workforce reduction was disclosed to the SEC four months before this posting was live
GAAP losses widened again in FY2025 after narrowing in FY2024, and the company names this first among its own risks
Hiring and cutting simultaneously means the roles that survive are the ones aligned to the new operating model — ask which this is
Two-thirds of open roles are Hybrid or In-Office; remote flexibility appears to be narrowing

questions_to_ask: Was this team affected by the May 2026 reduction, and is this role a backfill or new headcount?
What does 'agentic AI-first operating model' change about how this team actually works day to day?
Which of the public repositories does this team own, and what share of the work lands in them?
What is the on-call rotation depth for this service after the reduction?
